messages:
maya: quick idea: convert onboarding from a linear pipeline to a lightweight DAG where each step is an idempotent node with explicit inputs/outputs. avoids rerunning unrelated benches.

ravi: sounds promising. quick question: how do we prevent DAG explosion if we create tiny nodes for every small transform?

maya: plan: coarse-grain nodes by semantic role (compat, export, quantize, bench-fast, bench-full, packaging). not one file-per-op. keep node boundaries logical so the graph stays readable.

chris: bench-fast vs bench-full split is neat. bench-fast would catch basic perf regressions, bench-full runs golden suite. how do we escalate?

maya: bench-fast emits a "suspicion" score. if above threshold, enqueue bench-full on same model-variant. else mark pass. default thresholds configurable per customer tier.

lin: compatibility checks need to be early and cheap. propose a CI-style lint node that validates ABI (shapes, ops), tokenizer compatibility, and a quick smoke gen. Fail fast.

maya: exactly. the compatibility node returns a token like COMPAT_OK:true or fail with error codes: OP_MISSING, TOKENIZER_MISMATCH, SHAPE_MISMATCH. downstream nodes gate on that token.

kevin: caching/storage question: per-node artifacts mean more objects. what's TTL strategy?
maya: keep artifacts for 30 days by default, with policy to retain last N per model-family. compressed with zstd. also GC heuristics: if artifact reused by >=2 models in 30d, bump retention.

admit-bot: note: current linear intake averages ~38m. splitting into DAG might reduce avg rework by ~40% in our sim.

ravi: scheduler complexity is the main downside. do we build on our existing job runner or introduce a DAG orchestrator (airflow style)?

maya: prefer augmenting current runner with a DAG layer (lightweight orchestrator) instead of full airflow. we only need topological exec, cache lookup, and retry semantics. simpler to maintain.

chris: observability: need node-level traces, per-node latency histograms, and a provenance blob showing inputs that produced each artifact. UI should allow clicking a node to rerun just that node.

maya: +1. also add flakiness counters for bench nodes (variance over runs) so we can auto-flag flaky benches and quarantine them.

lin: how do we handle conditional branches (e.g., quantized path vs fp32 path)?

maya: nodes declare outputs tagged by variant. conditional edges reference variant predicates. scheduler materializes only the relevant subgraph.

kevin: rollout integrations? we need the final gate to produce a bundle that rollout-controller can consume (artifact refs + quality delta).

maya: final gate emits a signed manifest with artifact refs, deltas vs baseline, and quality verdict. rollout-controller can pull that and decide canary percentage.

ravi: any attack surface or security concerns with cached artifacts? signed manifests and KMS for artifact metadata?

maya: yes, sign manifests and optionally encrypt sensitive artifacts. add ACLs for artifact access.

chris: ok ready to review RFC. can you include an example node manifest and simple scheduler state machine?

maya: will do. PoC plan: 1) node manifest schema, 2) cache lookup + skip logic, 3) bench-fast integration, 4) UI mock for graph. goal: PoC in 3 weeks. reviewers: @ravi @chris @lin @kevin.

ravi: I'll review the schema.

lin: can help mock the compatibility lint.

kevin: will do storage numbers + cost model.

chris: I'll wire the bench-fast hooks.

maya: thanks all. I'll drop RFC link soon. :rocket:
